{{External|rs|dw}} {{Skill table links}} {{Has skill guide|members=Slayer training|iron=Ironman Guide/Slayer|UIM=Ultimate Ironman Guide/Slayer}} {{Infobox Skill |name = Slayer |image = [[File:Slayer icon.png]] |release = [[26 January]] [[2005]] |update = Slayer Skill |members = Yes |type = Utility }} [[File:Slayer icon (detail).png|left]] '''Slayer''' is a [[skill]] that allows players to kill [[Slayer monster]]s that may otherwise be untargetable by players (players would be prompted with a message stating they do not possess the required Slayer level to attack the monster). Players must visit a [[Slayer Master]], who will assign them a [[Slayer task|task]] to kill certain monsters based on the player's [[Combat level]]. Slayer [[experience]] is awarded each time the player kills an assigned monster, and is equal to the monster's [[Hitpoints]] multiplied by its [[experience bonus]]. Many players primarily train [[Combat]] by completing [[Slayer task]]s, as Combat experience is still given as normal while fighting [[Slayer monsters]]. At higher levels, Slayer becomes more profitable, as higher-levelled slayer monsters tend to have more lucrative drops both in common and uniques. Some [[boss]]es are additionally unique to Slayer and can only be killed when assigned it or their lesser category as an assignment. After completing a set amount of tasks, players will begin to earn [[slayer reward point]]s, which can be used for a wide array of purposes, such as beneficial buffs on specific tasks or some cosmetics. {{Listen |align = right |title = [[Slayer Level Up!]] |filename = Slayer Level Up!.ogg |desc = The music that plays when levelling up.}} {{Listen |align = right |title = [[Slayer Level Up! (Unlocks)]] |filename = Slayer Level Up! (Unlocks).ogg |desc = The music that plays when levelling up and unlocking new content.}} ==Introduction== A good in-game introduction to Slayer is provided by the [[A Porcine of Interest]] quest. To receive a [[Slayer task]], players must visit one of ten [[Slayer Master]]s throughout [[Gielinor]]. All but two Slayer Masters have a [[Combat level]] requirement, and the final Slayer Master also has a Slayer level requirement. The tasks assigned are generally appropriate for the Combat level of the player, assuming they use the highest level Master available. Players may be assigned normal monsters to kill, or they may be assigned monsters that require the use of Slayer-specific [[Slayer equipment|items]] to deal damage or Slayer-specific [[armour]] to prevent stat reduction. The [[Slayer equipment]] necessary to kill Slayer monsters can be purchased from any Slayer Master. When you get your task, you can ask the Master for advice on killing the assigned monsters, and they will tell you if special equipment is required. If no special equipment is necessary, they will give you other tips or advice such as if the monster is weak to [[poison]] or [[Magic]]. Players can check on the current status of their task through various items; beginners will likely be introduced to the [[enchanted gem]], which can be used to contact Slayer masters and provide information about task progression. They cannot be used to get a new task from the Slayer master. Alternatively, a [[combat bracelet]] can be used, although it will only update task progression every ten kills made. After completing a task, the player is awarded slayer points (if they have built up a sufficient streak) and are advised to get a new task from the Slayer master. They will either need to return to them in person, or those with access to [[Astral Contact]] may telepathically communicate with them to get one. The Slayer masters vary in the level of difficulty of their assignments; several of them require certain combat levels, although players are able to toggle this on and off freely if they desire. If a player is unable to complete a task and cannot cancel it, they must go to [[Turael]]. Resetting a task this way will reset the slayer task streak to 0. Turael is additionally unable to reset a task if it is something that he assigns, such as [[kalphite]]s. Masters are shown on the [[map]] with a yellow skull [[File:Slayer Master icon.png]] [[icon]]. '''Note:''' Skipping assignments through Turael is '''not''' a recommended choice, as it's better to gain [[Slayer points]] from doing tasks in a row and spending it on blocking or skipping your current task without breaking your task streak, as Slayer points also allow you to buy useful items and perks. ==Slayer Masters== A handful of [[Slayer Master]]s dot the map; each Master gives assignments oriented towards a general range of [[Combat level]]s. {| class="wikitable align-center-2 align-center-4" width="100%" !Name !Image !Location !Requirements !Details |- |[[Turael]]||[[File:Turael.png|85x150px]] |{{Map|name=Slayer|x=2932|y=3537|plane=0|r=3|height=200|width=200|mtype=square}} |None |''South-east [[Burthorpe]] - [[Games necklace]] teleport or [[Hot-air balloon]]'' [[Turael]]'s [[Slayer task|tasks]] are simple, small, and easy to find. These assignments are excellent for the Slayer with a low combat level, but his assignments yield such low experience that most players find him unsatisfactory. However, Turael is willing to replace an assignment given by another Slayer Master with an easier one, if the task to be replaced wouldn't normally be given by him (for example, he will replace a player's [[Black demon]] task but not a [[Crawling Hand]] task). This ability results in more players using his services than normally would. |''[[Wyrmscraig Cavern]], near the [[mooring point]]'' - [[Teleport to boat]], [[Slayer ring]], [[Necklace of passage]], or [[Ardeaglais teleport]] [[Mortimer]] is the most difficult [[Slayer Master]]. His assignments exclusively focus on monsters with [[superior slayer monster|superior variants]]. Unlike other Slayer Masters, Mortimer offers a choice between multiple task options, initially 2, but increasing to 3 after 50 completed tasks from him. These tasks provide special [[Mortimer#Tasks|modifiers]], offering certain bonuses. However, his tasks are more expensive to skip, only offer 2 block slots, and cannot be replaced by taking an assignment from [[Turael]]. Mortimer's tasks have a separate task completion counter from other Slayer Masters, and only give reward points if a points modifier is chosen. |} ==Slayer equipment== {{Main|Slayer equipment}} Various monsters encountered on [[Slayer task]]s require the use of specific [[Slayer equipment]], such as the [[earmuffs]] or a [[Leaf-bladed weapons|leaf-bladed weapon]]. Without the right equipment, it may become impossible for a player to finish their task. Some monsters could quickly deal large amounts of damage to players that aren't properly equipped, such as the [[dust devil]]s, while other monsters will simply not go down without the right tool, such as [[lizard]]s. It's therefore important to do some prior research before heading off to Slayer task you have never done before. [[Slayer master]]s will be able to sell you most of the available slayer equipment. They will also usually tell you what equipment you require when you receive a task from them. The [[black mask]] provides a bonus to damage and accuracy against assigned monsters on a Slayer task. It is generally the most useful headpiece to wear on any Slayer task besides the [[Slayer helmet]]. This helmet, unlocked with the ''[[Malevolent Masquerade]]'' reward, combines the abilities of the black mask along with several other pieces of Slayer equipment into one, and is therefore commonly worn by players on tasks. ==Slayer tasks== {{Main|Slayer tasks}} There's a wide variety of monsters that can be assigned as a [[Slayer task]] by the above [[Slayer master]]s. These may be either [[Slayer monsters]], which require a certain Slayer level to kill, or regular monsters such as [[Demon (race)|demons]], [[Dragon (race)|dragons]], and [[Giant (race)|giants]]. There are also various bosses that can be slain on a Slayer task. ===Bosses=== {{Main|Boss Slayer}} Some tasks have qualifying [[boss]] monsters. For example, players assigned to kill [[hellhound]]s can either choose to kill regular hellhounds or [[Cerberus]], the hellhound boss, granted players have the required Slayer level of 91 to slay her. Additionally, players who have unlocked the ''[[Boss#Boss slayer|Like a boss]]'' perk for 200 [[Slayer reward points]] may be directly assigned to slay a boss by [[Nieve]]/[[Steve]], [[Duradel]]/[[Kuradal]], or [[Konar quo Maten]]. [[Krystalia]] may also do this, but will assign bosses found in the [[Wilderness]]. Only bosses from [[Boss Slayer|this list]] that the player meets all requirements for may be assigned. When a boss is assigned, the allow the player to choose the number of bosses they wish to kill for that task. This number can be anywhere between 3 and 35, increased to a maximum of 65 through [[Combat Achievements]]. In case the [[Barrow brothers]] are assigned, the player may choose to slay 36 to accommodate for the number of brothers, even without any Combat Achievements. Completing an assigned boss task will grant an additional 5,000 Slayer experience after the task is complete. If looking to benefit from the use of a [[Slayer helmet]] while hunting items from a boss, standard tasks such as [[araxyte]]s are often preferable to boss-specific tasks such as [[Araxxor]], as they generally require more kills. Conversely, killing a boss during a boss-specific task may result in more Slayer experience per hour than a standard task due to the bonus experience awarded when the task is finished. ==Slayer Partners== [[File:Slayer Partner interface.png|thumb|right|The interface shown when selecting ''Partner''.]] Slayer Partners is a feature that allows up to two players to work together on the same [[slayer task]]. There are a few restrictions on the tasks you may receive, but players of any combat and slayer level may become partners. [[Ironman Mode|Ironmen]] are unable to use this feature, unless participating within a [[Group Ironman]] team. ===Assigning a partner=== You may invite a player to become your slayer partner by using the ''Partner'' function on an [[enchanted gem]], [[eternal gem]], or an equipped [[slayer ring]] or [[slayer helmet]]. When you use this feature, neither you nor the player you invite may currently have an active task assigned. Additionally, neither of you can have an open offer for a task from [[Mortimer]]. Players remain each other's partner even when logging out. Players can dismiss their partner at any time by using opening up the ''Partner'' interface again. Receiving a new task while your partner is offline or in another world will also end the partnership, though you'll receive a message warning you if this were about to happen. ===Receiving a task=== Once you have successfully assigned a partner, only one of you needs to talk to a slayer master for a new task. You will then both receive exactly the same assignment, individually. There are a few restrictions on which tasks the two of you may receive: * Both players must have the requirements to complete the same task. For example, you will not receive [[frost dragon]]s until both of you have 87 [[Sailing]] and a [[combat level]] of 85. ** This does not apply to [[Mortimer]] assigned tasks. If the player being assigned the task is not paying attention or does not know the requirements of a monster, an undoable option for their partner can be chosen. * Only the block list and the [[Slayer Rewards#Rewards|Slayer Reward]] unlocks{{fact|needs testing, seems like both people don't need the unlock if they both have the ability to do the task (ex: tzhaars)}} of the player who requests the task are taken into account. * Even if both players have unlocked [[Slayer Rewards|"Hot Stuff"]], they may receive the [[TzHaar]] task but will not be offered to slay [[TzTok-Jad]] or [[TzKal-Zuk]] instead. * Finally, there must be at least 15 tasks that can be assigned under the above circumstances. Otherwise, no task will be assigned, and the partners must visit another slayer master or somehow unlock more tasks. Either player may cancel, block, or store the active task at any time, though doing so only affects their own assignment. This means that the other player may still complete the task on their end. Note that stored tasks will no longer count as partner tasks when unstored. ===Getting kills=== As long as both slayer partners remain within 30 tiles of each other on the same world, the slayer kill count will be shared between them. You'll receive an in-game message when you kill an assigned slayer target while your partner is too far away, unless it was a monster killed in a solo [[instance|private instance]], such as [[Brutus]]. If one of the partners has already completed their task, e.g. by getting kills after the other player logged out, they can no longer contribute to the kill count of the other player's assignment. They could, however, still wound a monster, allowing their partner to finish it for the kill. Slayer experience gained for killing a monster remains unaffected. As with regular slayer tasks, you'll receive only half of the experience of a monster you kill if your partner or another player has dealt over half the damage to it. If [[expeditious bracelet]]s or [[bracelets of slaughter]] are worn when experience for killing a monster is split between you and your partner, the bracelets of both players can activate on the same monster kill. ===Reward points=== Upon completing a partner task, players receive a number of [[slayer reward point]]s proportional to the number of monsters they have killed themself. For example, a task from [[Duradel]] would normally reward 15 points upon completion. If you've killed roughly 60% of the monsters on your task yourself, you'll receive 9 points (60% of 15 points). In the rare case you've killed exactly 50% of the monsters, you'll receive 8 points (instead of 7), because the number of points will be rounded up. The number of points you receive is not affected by the number of monster kills your partner has contributed to their own task. In other words, if their monster kill count wasn't fully shared with you (e.g. due to moving too far away), the combined number of kills between you will be higher, because you'll have to kill one or more additional monsters yourself. This makes it possible for both of you to receive more than 50% of the regular reward points. Task streaks are counted individually for each player, and milestone bonuses are seperated from the regular reward points on partner tasks. For example, completing an assignment from Duradel as the 10th slayer task in a row normally grants you 75 reward points if done alone. If done with a partner, you'll instead receive 60 points as a streak bonus and up to 15 points from the shared task. If a player hasn't killed at least 20% of the monsters on their task, they will not receive any reward points and their task will not count towards their streak. ====Example==== Both you and your slayer partner have received a task to slay 150 [[Slayer task/Elves|elves]] from [[Duradel]]. Working together to share the kill count, you manage to kill 70 elves while your partner kills 50. * You both have 120/150 kills counted for the slayer task. Your partner logs out, and while they are away you kill 30 elves. You receive 10 reward points for completing your task. * Killing 100 of the 150 elves counted towards your slayer task gives you 2/3 of the 15 maximum reward points. Your partner still needs to kill an additional 30 elves to complete their task. * The kill count cannot be shared anymore, since you already finished your task. Your partner receives 68 reward points (8 + 60). *Killing 80 of the 150 elves counted towards their slayer task gives them 8/15 of the 15 maximum reward points. *As this was your partner's 10th completed task in a row, they receive an additional 60 reward points as a streak bonus. ==Slayer reward points== {{main|Slayer reward point}} Slayer reward points may be earned after having completed five tasks in a row without having a task changed by [[Turael]]. However, players may cancel a task by spending 30 points. '''Tip''': You may want to use an [[expeditious bracelet]] to complete the first five tasks faster. Points can be spent at any [[Slayer rewards]] shop on items and unlocks including unlocking new monsters as a Slayer task, a [[Slayer ring]], the ability to combine all Slayer headgear into one item, the [[Slayer helmet]], and even the ability to prevent players from being assigned a specific task forever. Since getting good tasks worth keeping isn't guaranteed, it is suggested that players get their first four assignments from the Slayer Master [[Turael]], and then get any other assignments from higher Masters like [[Duradel]]. After getting five or more tasks in a row, Slayer Masters will hand out points when players finish their tasks. The number of points varies as the difficulty of the Slayer Master increases. Every 10th, 50th, 100th, 250th, and 1,000th task, a special bonus is given to the player's Slayer reward points, the bonuses also differ in points to each Slayer Master. Whenever a task is done the player will be notified on what number task it is, and the total amount of points they have. This can help players plan to what Slayer Master they prefer to go next, to maximise the number of Slayer reward points in the shortest amount of time. {| class="wikitable" !Master !Location !Points given per completed Task !Points per 10th !Points per 50th !Points per 100th !Points per 250th !Points per 1,000th |- |[[Turael]] / [[Aya]] |[[Burthorpe]] opposite the pub to the east |N/A |N/A |N/A |N/A |N/A |N/A |- |[[Spria]] |[[Draynor Village]] |N/A |N/A |N/A |N/A |N/A |N/A |- |[[Mazchna]] / [[Achtryn]] |North-east of [[Canifis]] |6 |30 |90 |150 |210 |300 |- |[[Vannaka]] |North-east area of [[Edgeville Dungeon]] |8 |40 |120 |200 |280 |400 |- |[[Chaeldar]] |Throne room in [[Zanaris]] |10 |50 |150 |250 |350 |500 |- |[[Nieve]] / [[Steve]] |At the [[Tree Gnome Stronghold]], south-west of the [[Spirit tree]] |12 (15)Completion of the Elite [[Western Provinces Diary]] increases the Slayer reward points to match those of [[Duradel]]. |60 (75) |180 (225) |300 (375) |420 (525) |600 (750) |- |[[Duradel]] / [[Kuradal]] |On the roof of the Fishing store in [[Shilo Village (location)|Shilo Village]] |15 |75 |225 |375 |525 |750 |- |[[Konar quo Maten]] |[[Mount Karuulm]] |18 (20)Completion of the Elite [[Kourend & Kebos Diary]] increases the Slayer reward points obtained. |90 (100) |270 (300) |450 (500) |630 (700) |900 (1,000) |- |[[Krystilia]] |Jailhouse north-east of [[Edgeville]] bank |25 |125 |375 |625 |875 |1,250 |- |[[Mortimer]] |Next to the [[Mooring point]] in the [[Wyrmscraig Cavern]] |0-40Mortimer's tasks only grant points if the task has a points modifier. Points can vary depending on task, and are not increased by milestones. |N/A |N/A |N/A |N/A |N/A |} After earning enough points, players will be able to buy rewards with earned points. (See [[Slayer reward point|main article]] for more details) The [[Slayer helmet]] combines the stat boosting qualities of the [[Black mask]] with the protective Slayer headgear [[facemask]], [[nosepeg]], [[earmuffs]], [[reinforced goggles]] (should the player have finished [[A Porcine of Interest]]), and [[Spiny helmet]], with the defence bonuses of a [[rune full helm]], making it the best melee helmet option for slayers. This allows for monsters like [[aberrant spectres]] and [[dust devils]] to be killed while having the bonuses of the 15% Attack and Strength increase. Players can also imbue their Slayer helmets via the [[Nightmare Zone]], [[Emir's Arena]] or [[Soul Wars]]. This gives all the bonuses of the Slayer helmet, while boosting Ranged and Magic by 15% as well. The Slayer helmet's effects '''do not''' stack with a [[salve amulet]] or [[salve amulet (e)]] for a bonus on [[Undead|undead creatures]], such as aberrant spectres. The Slayer helmet has a better bonus so it is recommended just to wear the Slayer helmet and an amulet of your choice (unless you have yet to unlock the ability to create the helmet and use the nose peg for example; then a salve amulet is recommended). ==Collection log== {{Main|Slayer/Collection log}} There is a wide range of [[Slayer/Collection log|collection log]] items related to the Slayer skill. This generally includes unique drops from monsters that can be assigned as a [[Slayer task]] and weren't given an individual collection log page, such as the [[elemental gems]]. There isn't any reward for obtaining collection log items other than the [[Collection log#Ranks|staves of collection]], although numerous players still enjoy collecting them as a sense of completion. Additionally, several of these items have a high value on the [[Grand Exchange]], and some may be especially sought after by [[Ironman Mode|Ironmen]] due to their trade restrictions, such as the [[abyssal whip]] or [[imbued heart]]. ==Temporary boosts== {{main|Temporary skill boost}} {{:Temporary skill boost/Slayer}} ==Quests== {{Sync}} ===Quests requiring Slayer=== {| class="wikitable sortable qc-active lighttable mw-collapsible" style="text-align:center;" !Quest !Slayer

Later on in the [[April 2023 Game Jam#Slayer Improvements|April 2023 Game Jam]], a Group Slayer system was developed which could both function in the [[Group Ironman Mode]] as well as replace the original Slayer Partner system. Later, in a [[Update:Re-introducing: Slayer Partners|blogpost]] on [[1 August]] [[2024]], there were plans made to re-introduce the Slayer partner system, with new restrictions to reduce the possibilities of abuse. Finally on [[14 August]] [[2024]], the Slayer partner system was reintroduced with several major changes to receiving and completing a task with a partner. ==See also== * [[Slayer/Experience table]], a list of all Slayer experience sources from monsters * [[Slayer/Level up table]], a list of all requirements and unlockables within the Slayer skill {{Skills}} [[Category:Members' skills]]
